title: Yahoo Finance Morning Brief: January 29, 2019
text:
Tuesday, January 29, 2019
Get the Morning Brief sent directly to your inbox every Monday to Friday by 6:30 a.m. ET. Subscribe
WHAT TO WATCH Tech behemoth Apple ( AAPL ) will take center stage when it reports Q4 financial results after the market close. The iPhone maker has been thrust into the spotlight this year after it slashed its revenue guidance for Q4, citing weak iPhone sales in China. As Apple gears up to report on Tuesday, the outlook remains bleak among market watchers. Analysts polled by Bloomberg are expecting Apple to report earnings of $4.17 per share on $83.97 billion of revenue for Q4.
Earnings continue to roll out with 3M ( MMM ), Allergan ( AGN ), Biogen ( BIIB ), Harley-Davidson ( HOG ), Lockheed Martin ( LMT ), Pfizer ( PFE ), PulteGroup ( PHM ) and Verizon ( VZ ) reporting before market open. Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ), Amgen ( AMGN ) and eBay ( EBAY ) will round things out after the market close.
Additionally, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) two-day meeting kicks off today.

TOP NEWS The logo for Pacific Gas & Electric Co. appears above a trading post on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange, Monday, Jan. 14, 2019. PG&E lost half its value after the troubled California utility, which faces huge liabilities over the state's deadly wildfires, said it would file for bankruptcy protection. (AP Photo/Richard Drew) More PG&E files for bankruptcy : Power provider PG&E Corp. ( PCG ) filed for voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection on Tuesday, succumbing to liabilities stemming from wildfires in Northern California in 2017 and 2018. The owner of the biggest U.S. power utility has filed a motion seeking court approval for a $5.5 billion debtor-in-possession financing, it said in a statement. [Reuters]
U.S. charges China's Huawei and its CFO : The United States on Monday announced criminal charges against China's Huawei Technologies Co. Ltd., escalating a fight with the world's biggest telecommunications equipment maker and coming days before trade talks between Washington and Beijing. The Justice Department charged Huawei and its chief financial officer, Meng Wanzhou, with conspiring to violate U.S. sanctions on Iran by doing business with Tehran through a subsidiary it tried to hide. [Reuters]
Trump slaps de-facto oil ban on Venezuela .:The Trump administration dealt its toughest blow yet to the authoritarian Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro, issuing new sanctions on the nation’s state-owned oil company PDVSA that effectively block his regime from exporting crude to the U.S. [Bloomberg]
Wynn to settle founder's sexual misconduct claims: Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) said it has agreed to an undisclosed settlement in response to a disciplinary complaint filed by the Nevada Gaming Control Board following a series of sexual misconduct claims against former chief executive Steve Wynn. [Reuters]
